idiom_name: Twirl templates compiled to Scala functions (@views.html.partials.row(p), @main(...){...})
implementation_notes: Play's Twirl compiles every app/views/*.scala.html template into a Scala object exposing a typed render/apply method, so the layout is a template that takes the page body as a parameter (typically a second argument list receiving Html) and a fragment is called like a function - @views.html.partials.productRow(product) inside a @for loop, or helper templates under views/helpers that take plain values. Templates can also inject collaborators with @this(...) before the parameter list. This replaces a runtime include mechanism with ordinary typed function calls, at the cost of a compile step for every markup change; ScalaTags/HTML-DSL composition is the same idea with markup as Scala code.
pitfalls: Every template is compiled, so markup changes invalidate a build and hot-reload setups must run the Twirl compile step on save.
Rendered fragments are Html values: passing and calling them keeps escaping intact, while wrapping concatenated strings in @Html(...) bypasses it.
A template's parameter list is the fragment's interface - adding an argument breaks every caller at compile time (good) but creates churn across the views package.
